# BHI260AP firmware images

The part runs whatever firmware the host uploads into its RAM at start-up, so
"which firmware" is a choice made on this side, not a property of the board.

**Only one image is loaded at a time, and they trade features.** There is no
combining KLIO learning with data injection on this silicon.

## `bhi260_klio.img` — the default, generated by `fetch.sh`

123,708 bytes. Bosch's KLIO image: 35 virtual sensors, gesture learning and
recognition, orientation, gyro. This is what the IMU window, the posture
vocabulary and `klio` all need.

## `DataInject.fw` / `DataInject_nobsx.fw` — Bosch's diagnostic firmware

95,960 and 94,460 bytes, taken **unmodified** from Bosch's own repository:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boschsensortec/BHI2xy_SensorAPI/master/firmware/bhi260ap/DataInject.fw
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boschsensortec/BHI2xy_SensorAPI/master/firmware/bhi260ap/DataInject_nobsx.fw
```

`nobsx` is the same image without the BSX fusion algorithms.

**This is the firmware that makes host-supplied motion possible**, and its
existence was not obvious: SensorLib (the Arduino library this port originally
took its firmware from) carries only the KLIO and shuttle variants for the 260,
so it looks as though Bosch never built injection for this part. They did.

What it costs: **only two virtual sensors, ids 4 and 6** — the accelerometer and
its wake-up variant. No gyro, no orientation, no KLIO. The IMU window and the
KLIO experiments do not work while this is loaded.

### Flashing it

The image has to go into the port's own wrapper first — a 12-byte header
(`FUMI`, payload length, first four bytes of the SHA-256 of the payload) before
Bosch's bytes, which is what `fetch.sh` builds for the KLIO image:

```python
import struct, hashlib
fw = open("DataInject.fw","rb").read()
hdr = struct.pack('<III', 0x494D5546, len(fw),
                  int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(fw).digest()[:4], 'little'))
open("DataInject.img","wb").write(hdr + fw)
```

then

```
esptool write_flash 0xE10000 DataInject.img
```

and to go back:

```
esptool write_flash 0xE10000 bhi260_klio.img
```

`imu boot` reports the part's own verdict without needing a working image, and
`imu boot upload` sends whatever is at `moddata+0x10000` and prints the boot
status afterwards. **`boot 38` is a good boot** (`iface-ready verify-done
no-flash`); **`boot 78` with `err 14` is a rejected image** — which is exactly
what the BHI360 image does, see below.


## THE ARCHITECTURE, AND IT IS THE POINT (entry 57)

**A DataInject image is an algorithm PLUS injection — not an accelerometer faker.**
This is what Bosch's own example does and it took a while to see:

```
examples/swim/swim_data_injection/swim_data_injection.c
  #define CUSTOM_SENSOR_ID  BHY2_SENSOR_ID_SWIM        /* 114, an ALGORITHM */
  firmware/bhi260ap_swim/DataInject_nobsx.fw           /* a DIFFERENT folder */
```

They inject a recorded motion log and read the **algorithm's** output. Injected
data replaces the algorithm's *input*; the algorithm then runs on it. Feeding a
physical sensor's output is not what this family is for, which is why
`bhi260ap/DataInject.fw` — whose only sensors are 4 and 6 — accepted data and
emitted a constant payload no matter what was sent.

Measured on the glass, all three images:

```
bhi260ap/DataInject.fw       95,960 B   booted   sensors 4 6          <- no algorithm
bhi260ap_swim/DataInject_nobsx.fw 104,700 B  booted  sensors 3 8 12 17 **114**
bhi260ap_klio/...            123,696 B  booted   sensors ... 112 127  <- no injection
```

**`DataInject_SWIM.fw` in this directory is the one that carries an algorithm
(114, SWIM) and boots on this board.** It is the proof that the pipeline the
operator wants exists on this silicon: host sine in, algorithm consumes it,
answer out.

**There is no public KLIO + DataInject image.** Bosch publishes KLIO
(`bhi260ap_klio/`, learning and recognition, no injection) and separately
injection builds carrying SWIM or nothing. Combining them is a toolchain build,
not a download.

### What the feeder established before stopping

`imu feed` now injects and round-trips without wedging — 199 to 299 events out
for 200 to 300 injections, **exactly one event per injection**, which shows the
part pacing itself off host data. The *values* never came through: every payload
decoded as `00 08 00 01 00 00 00` regardless of input, and identically for event
ids 4, 55 and 76. That is consistent with the image having no algorithm to
consume them.

### Three instrument bugs fixed on the way, each of which had cost a hard reset

1. **`bhy2.c parse_fifo()` span for ever on a sensor id with `event_size == 0`** —
   `read_pos += 0` never advances, no I2C traffic, no output, indistinguishable
   from a hang. Now skips one byte. This is the wedge that killed `imu feed` and
   every `imu raw` before it.
2. **`imu raw` read a 4-byte header from data FIFOs**, which have a 2-byte
   length; only the status channel has the 4-byte header. That reported an empty
   FIFO as "251 bytes waiting" and dumped zeros.
3. **`imu raw` capped partial FIFO reads**, desynchronising the stream for every
   later read (a header went on to claim 64,768 bytes). It now refuses rather
   than reads short.

## The BHI360 images do NOT work — measured, not assumed

Bosch ships `firmware/bhi360/bosch_data_inject_bhi360.h` and BHy2CLI targets the
BHI360/BHI385. Those images share our container magic (`0x662B`) and their
payload is a plausible size, so they look plausible. They are not:

```
BHI260AP KLIO        123,696 B   booted       boot 38  err 00
BHI360 data_inject    99,736 B   VERIFY-ERROR boot 78  err 14
```

The part received the BHI360 image in full, ran verification and rejected it.
Chip id is the reason: **BHI260 = 0x70, BHI360 = 0x7A**, and this board reports
0x70.

## The injection protocol, from Bosch's own example

`examples/swim/swim_data_injection/swim_data_injection.c` in
`boschsensortec/BHI2xy_SensorAPI`. Every step below was missing from this port's
earlier attempts:

```
1  bhy2_set_data_injection_mode(STEP_BY_STEP)
2  bhy2_set_virt_sensor_cfg(SENSOR_ID, rate, latency)   <-- CONFIGURE FIRST
3  drain the status FIFO
4  bhy2_inject_data(timestamp, 6)    a full timestamp, its OWN call
5  bhy2_inject_data(event, 7)        then one FIFO event (id + 3 x int16)
6  drain the FIFO between injections
```

**Step 2 is the one that explains every earlier failure.** Injection supplies
data *for a virtual sensor*; with no sensor configured nothing is listening, so
the packets are accepted and dropped — which is exactly what
`DATA INJECTION — SETTLED` recorded on the KLIO image.

The port implements this as `imu feed <seconds> <hz> <amp>`, which generates a
sine, injects it and round-trips the samples back through the part's parser.

**It is NOT yet proven: the command wedges the shell task on the drain**, and
`imu raw` on a FIFO channel desyncs the stream when the read is capped short of
the stated length. Both are instrument bugs, not conclusions about the part.
